title: Spike: Link clock from apricity serve to an AudioWorklet: accuracy per browser, reachability from the cloud app
description:
## Intent
Answer M0 question 6: can a web page follow a Link session through `apricity serve`, and how closely?

## Steps (throwaway)
1. A tiny native process joins Link and serves a WebSocket on 127.0.0.1 sending `{tempo, beat, serverMicros, playing, peers}` every 20 ms and answering `ping`.
2. A test page estimates the clock offset from ping/pong (keep the lowest round trips), maps server time to `performance.now()` and then to `AudioContext` time with `getOutputTimestamp()` and `outputLatency`, and schedules a click on every beat in an AudioWorklet.
3. Measure the error in Chrome, Safari and Firefox on macOS by recording the output against a reference peer's clicks (loopback driver or a second recording path): p99 and max, with and without a background tab.
4. From the cloud app's origin (https): can the page open `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>`? Record per browser (mixed content, Private Network Access). Share the finding with apricitus-92b5b5.

## Leaves
A comment with the per-browser numbers and a recommendation: which browsers are supported, whether cloud mode can use Link, the ping rate and the offset filter.

## Verify
The comment holds a table: browser, p99 ms, max ms, background-tab behavior, cloud-origin reachability.

Labels `daw`, `web`. Commit: none (spike).
